newsitem.title: INDIA: P&G launches "new, improved" India detergent.
newsitem.headline: P&G launches "new, improved" India detergent.

text.p: Procter & Gamble Home Products Ltd, the wholly-owned Indian subsidiary of Procter & Gamble Company (P&G) of the U.S. said it relaunched its Ariel detergent with a new ingredient used for the first time by P&G worldwide.
The relaunched Ariel uses an organic dispersant "Microshine" patented by the U.S. parent in 1995, said N.V.Iyer, head of laundry research and development of the Indian firm.
The chemical disperses dirt and prevents it reattaching to the fabric after washing. It is far superior to conventional dispersants now used in India, Iyer said.
"It was invented by P&G's laboratory in Cincinnati," said Iyer. P&G's Indian arm developed the formula, which officials said would also be used in P&G's other firms all over the world.

Alex Howson, category manager, laundry and cleaning products at Procter & Gamble Home Products, said the Ariel brand (including powder and scrubbing bar) had an eight percent share of the Indian detergent market. The market is dominated by Unilever subsididary Hindustan Lever.
The relaunched Ariel carries an endorsement by Vimal, the textile division of India's textile and petrochemicals maker Reliance Industries Ltd.
Procter & Gamble launched Ariel as India's first compact (concentrated) detergent in 1990. Today, the compact market is valued at 3.0 billion rupees, P&G officials said.
"This market is growing at 10 percent compared with the rest of the detergent market at 2.0 percent," said Nayantara Bali, marketing manager (laundry and cleaning products).
"Even the poorest recognise the value of (product) performance," Bali said. She said single-use sachet packs constituted almost half the sales in compact detergents.
